literal: Any country indeed becomes [his own], any town indeed becomes [his own]; why does a person, until dying, remain without learning?
translation: Since every country and every town becomes a learned person's own, why does anyone remain unlearned until their death?
modern: கற்றவனுக்கு எந்த நாடும் தன் நாடாகும், எந்த ஊரும் தன் ஊராகும்; அப்படியிருக்க, ஒருவன் தன் இறப்பு வரைக்கும் கற்காமல் இருப்பது ஏன்?
explanation: This couplet highlights the universal acceptance and belonging that education brings to a person. A learned person is welcomed and respected everywhere, making any foreign country or town feel like their own home. Given this immense benefit of learning, which removes all geographical barriers, the poet questions why anyone would choose to remain uneducated throughout their entire life until death. The key words 'nāṭāmāl' (becomes one's country) and 'ūrāmāl' (becomes one's town) emphasize that knowledge grants global citizenship, making the refusal to learn ('kallāta āṟu') highly irrational.
